instruction: Rename the directory "todo_list_Jan_1" to "todo-list-Jan-1" on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: [ -d ~/Desktop/todo-list-Jan-1 ] && echo 'Directory exists.' || echo 'Directory does not exist.'

metadata.explanation: Task requires renaming directory by replacing underscores with dashes. Evaluator verifies that todo-list-Jan-1 exists. Uses existing exact_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Evaluator only checks that the NEW directory name 'todo-list-Jan-1' exists, but does NOT verify that the OLD directory 'todo_list_Jan_1' no longer exists
This creates a critical verification gap: a user could simply CREATE a new directory 'todo-list-Jan-1' instead of RENAMING the original 'todo_list_Jan_1', and the evaluator would still pass
A proper rename verification should check BOTH conditions: (1) new directory exists AND (2) old directory does not exist
The logic that IS present works correctly (checks directory existence at correct path with correct expected output), but it only verifies half of what a rename operation entails
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Modify the shell command to check both conditions: '[ -d ~/Desktop/todo-list-Jan-1 ] && [ ! -d ~/Desktop/todo_list_Jan_1 ] && echo 'Rename successful.' || echo 'Rename failed.'
Update expected value to match the new output: 'Rename successful.\n'
Alternative: Use two separate checks in the evaluator config to verify both the presence of new directory and absence of old directory
